# Decisions

Why the software is the way it is. Decisions are written down with their reasons, so that a new
request can be checked against them before anyone builds it, and so that nobody has to argue the
same question again next quarter.

## Two homes

| Where | Holds | Ids |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/decisions/NNNN-<title>.md` | Project-wide decisions: the stack, the defaults, the testing style, the language of code, junctions, and any decision that weighed real alternatives | `ADR-0007`: four digits, never reused |
| `.claude/skills/<context>/development/decisions.md` | One context's decisions, as an append-only log under an Active table | `billing-D3`: the context, `D`, a number never reused |

A context's Active table lists every decision that binds it today: its own entries, and links to
the ADRs that bind it. An ADR is linked, never copied.

## The entry

```markdown
### billing-D3 — Emails are unique regardless of case (2026-11-25)

Status: accepted · supersedes: billing-D1 · superseded by: —

In the context of registration, facing duplicate accounts, we decided for case-insensitive
uniqueness (and against exact matching), to achieve one identity per person, accepting a
migration of the existing rows.

Context: <the forces, described neutrally>
Options considered: <A, B: one line of pros and cons each>
Consequences: <good, bad, neutral>
Confirmation: scenario: "Registering twice with different casing is refused"; invariant: C3
Confidence: medium. Revisit when: <the change that would reopen it>
```

- **An ADR** carries every part, under a `#` title with its id: `# ADR-0007 — Title (date)`.
  Context, Options considered and Consequences may be `Name:` lines or, when they need room,
  `## Name` sections.
- **A context entry** needs at least the heading, the status line, the summary sentence and
  Confirmation.

## Confirmation

It ties a decision to something a machine can find, so that code drifting away from the decision
fails a check. Separate forms with `;`:

| Form | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `scenario: "<name>"` | A `Scenario:`, `Scenario Outline:` or `Example:` with that name in the context's `.feature` files; for an ADR, in any `.feature` file of the product |
| `test: <path> "<name>"` | A test with that name in that file |
| `invariant: C<n>`, `invariant: <context>/C<n>`, `invariant: M<n>` | An invariant in the context's `architecture.md`, in another context's, or in the module standard |

`node scripts/gyos-doctor.ts` checks that every Confirmation resolves.

**Invariant numbers are never reused or renumbered.** A retired invariant keeps its number, marked
retired, so that no Confirmation silently starts pointing at a different rule.

## Changing your mind

An accepted entry is never edited. Write a new one that supersedes it. Exactly two edits are
allowed afterwards:
- filling in the old entry's "superseded by";
- removing its row from the Active table.
